newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end higher, buoyed by demand for cash bonds.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end higher, buoyed by demand for cash bonds.

text.p: *Key March JGB futures ended higher, as cash bond buying by investors invited a spate of short-covering towards the close. *Japan's machinery orders fell 9.7 percent in November from the previous month, the EPA said. The figure was within expectations and had little effect on the market, traders said.

Japan's machinery orders are on a rising trend overall, an EPA official said on Thursday. The assessment was a slight improvement from the EPA's judgment in the previous month. Some said the machinery orders data was not a factor because the market was more concerned about the future than the current state of the economy.
A city bank trader said the market was not concerned even if the economy were recovering in the near-term, because it was interested in its longer-term prospects.
Investors were detected buying medium- and long-term bonds during the day, traders said.
Public funds were detected buying 10-year JGBs, a European bank trader said.
Some investors were detected selling JGBs with two- to three-year maturities ahead of a six-year bond auction scheduled on Friday, a trader at a city bank's securities affiliate said.
The Ministry of Finance said it would hold a six-year JGB auction on Friday. Traders said the offer volume was likely to be about 500 billion yen and the coupon rate 1.7 percent.
The benchmark 182nd cash JGB yield stood at 2.395 percent as of 0721 GMT, down from Tuesday's 2.435 percent.
In the morning session, the March contract ended slightly easier, after recouping most of its early losses.
The March's topside was weighed down early in the morning by the dollar's rise to a 46-month high against the yen overseas.
Traders said the March regained much of its early morning losses in the late morning on short-covering by dealers.
